headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most popular public APIs that will take an IP address and return the best‑available company / organization data (including contact details when the provider supplies them). All of them expose a simple **GET** endpoint that you can hit directly from your browser, curl, Postman, or any HTTP client library. | Service | Endpoint | Key Features | Typical Response | Notes | |---------|----------|--------------|------------------|-------| | **ipinfo.io** | `https://ipinfo.io//json?token=` | • Organization name
• ASN
• Company domain (if known)
• Contact email (via `org` field or `company` sub‑object) | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","hostname":"dns.google","city":"Mountain View","region":"California","country":"US","loc":"37.3860,-122.0840","org":"AS15169 Google LLC","postal":"94035","timezone":"America/Los_Angeles","readme":"https://ipinfo.io/missingauth"}``` | Free tier: 50k requests/month. Requires a token for production. | | **ipapi.com** | `https://ipapi.co//json/` | • Organization name
• Domain
• Company name
• Contact phone/email (via `org` field) | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","city":"Mountain View","region":"California","country_name":"United States","org":"Google LLC","postal":"94035","latitude":37.386,"longitude":-122.084,"timezone":"America/Los_Angeles","readme":"https://ipapi.co"} ``` | Free tier: 30k requests/day. No token needed for low volume. | | **ipdata.co** | `https://api.ipdata.co/?api-key=` | • Organization name
• Domain
• Company name
• Contact email & phone (via `company` object) | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","organization":"Google LLC","company":{"name":"Google LLC","domain":"google.com","email":"support@google.com","phone":"+1-650-253-0000"}}``` | Free tier: 1k requests/day. Requires API key. | | **ipstack.com** | `http://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=&format=1` | • Organization name
• Domain
• Company name
• Contact email (via `company` object) | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","location":{"country_name":"United States","region_name":"California","city":"Mountain View"},"company":{"name":"Google LLC","domain":"google.com","email":"support@google.com"}}``` | Free tier: 10k requests/month. Requires API key. | --- ## How to Use One of These APIs Below is a minimal example using **ipinfo.io** (the same pattern applies to the others). Replace `` with the target IP address and `` with your personal token. ```bash curl -s "https://ipinfo.io//json?token=" ``` ### Sample Response (JSON) ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "hostname": "dns.google", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country": "US", "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840", "org": "AS15169 Google LLC", "postal": "94035", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "readme": "https://ipinfo.io/missingauth" } ``` If the provider supplies a company object, you’ll see something like: ```json "company": { "name": "Google LLC", "domain": "google.com", "email": "support@google.com", "phone": "+1-650-253-0000" } ``` --- ## Quick Python Example (Using `requests`) ```python import requests def get_ip_company_info(ip, token): url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json" params = {"token": token} resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() data = resp.json() # Extract company info if present company = data.get("company", {}) org = data.get("org", "") return { "ip": data.get("ip"), "org": org, "company_name": company.get("name"), "domain": company.get("domain"), "email": company.get("email"), "phone": company.get("phone") } # Example usage if __name__ == "__main__": ip_address = "8.8.8.8" api_token = "YOUR_IPINFO_TOKEN" info = get_ip_company_info(ip_address, api_token) print(info) ``` --- ## Things to Keep in Mind | Issue | Recommendation | |-------|----------------| | **Rate limits** | All free tiers have limits (e.g., 50k/month for ipinfo.io). For production, consider upgrading or caching results. | | **Privacy** | Some IP addresses belong to private networks or VPNs; the returned data may be incomplete or generic. | | **Contact availability** | Not every IP will have a company or contact record. The API will simply omit those fields. | | **Legal compliance** | Ensure you comply with GDPR / CCPA when storing or displaying personal/company data. | --- ### TL;DR Pick one of the above services, sign up for a free API key (if required), and hit the endpoint with the IP address. The JSON payload will contain whatever company / organization data the provider has on file—often including a domain, email, and phone number. If you need higher volume or more detailed data, upgrade to a paid plan or combine multiple providers for redundancy.
